```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A shows documented willingness to pay at meaningful price points: Ello at $14.99/mo or $139/yr, Synthesis at about $119/yr, and Mentava at $500/mo. Idea B's price ceiling is $1-4/mo, so revenue per customer is far lower.",
    "Idea A's demand quotes come from parents describing the exact pain, including trying many tools and finding tutoring too expensive. Idea B's quotes are mostly about business inboxes, such as replying from info@ instead of an admin address, not the privacy-conscious multi-alias prosumer it targets.",
    "Idea B's core feature is already shipped by at least five competitors. Several include it free or bundled (addy.io, SimpleLogin, ProxiedMail), Maskwire sells it as a named $3/mo tool, and a free open-source Thunderbird extension solves the client-side case. That leaves little room for a standalone paid product.",
    "Idea A also faces free incumbents (Khan Academy Kids, Samio), but the brief names paths to differentiate, such as a niche bundle or struggling readers. Its price range is wide enough that a first paying customer within 90 days is plausible.",
    "Idea A's risks are real but bounded. COPPA setup has a clear one-time remedy (a legal consult on consent and privacy flows). Idea B's main risk is commoditization, which no setup step fixes."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's demand evidence. The three forum threads (Zoho, Apple, Microsoft) show general mail-client From-address annoyances, mostly in business-domain setups. None show the target segment (privacy prosumers with 10+ aliases) paying, or wanting to pay, for a standalone fix. The size of that segment is explicitly unknown, and the open-questions section defers to a field that is not present in the brief.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Idea A has its own gaps: the cost and conversion of the organic parenting-community channel are unsourced, COPPA compliance adds launch friction, and trust in children's products may build slowly. However, Idea B's combination of a commoditized, free-or-bundled feature and a sub-$4/mo price ceiling makes it the weaker first bet for reaching a paying customer within 90 days."
}
```
